8.text:
In a legal move the disc that is put down has to be on a line which is
closed on the other side by a disc of the player who moves.  On the
board that is printed the only white material which is closed on one
side by a black disc and which is open on the other side is the block

      F8 B   G8 B   H8 B   I8 B   J8 B
                     I9 W I10 W I11 W I12 B
                       J9 B J10 W J11 W J12 W J13 W J14 W J15 B
                          K8 W K9 W K10 W K11 W K12 W
                          L8 W L9 W L10 W L11 W L12 W
                              M8 B M9 W M10 W M11 W
                              N8 B N9 W N10 W N11 W

up to the usual Reversi convention.  In particular the 5–white
segment

      J9 B – J10 W – J11 W – J12 W – J13 W – J14 W – J15 B

is closed on the right by the black disc J15 and on the left by the
black disc J9.  The only empty square which is contiguous with the
segment and which closes it on the left is the square K7–L7–M7–N7–O7
in the 8th–column line

      J8 B – K8 W – L8 W – M8 B

and the 4–white line

      J9 B – K9 W – L9 W – M9 W – N9 W – O9 .

The common intersection of the two lines is the empty square

      K7

in the usual A1 notation.  Putting the black disc on K7 closes the
horizontal white line

     K8 W K9 W K10 W K11 W K12 W

on the right and the vertical white line

     K8 W L8 W

on the top and it closes the diagonal white line
K8 W–L9 W–M10 W–N11 W.  On the board as printed the longest closed
white line which can be closed in one move is the 12–white line

     J9 B – K9 W – L9 W – M9 W – N9 W – O9  B

together with the 5–white horizontal line K8–K12.  Up to the
conventional counting of the disc which is put down this is the
$12+1=13$–disc capture that is usually quoted as a 12–disc flip.  In
particular the essentially unique maximal capture is the 12 white
discs that are flipped on the K–row / 9–column cross, the 5–disc
horizontal capture K8–K12 and the 7–disc vertical/diagonal capture
K9–O9.  This is the well known 12–white, 13–stone, maximum of the
position; with the usual “flipped discs only’’ convention the maximum
number of white men that can be turned over in a single legal black
move is 12, i.e. 13 stones counting the move itself.  This is the
maximal capture of the position and, up to symmetry, the only
maximal capture.

2.text:
In a Reversi move a black stone may be put on an empty square $e$
and in every of the eight directions

$e,s_{1},s_{2},\dots ,s_{k},s_{k+1}$

$s_{1},\dots ,s_{k}$ are white and $s_{k+1}$ is black the $k$ white men
$s_{1},\dots ,s_{k}$ are turned over.  On the 20$\times$20 board which is
written out in the statement the only non–trivial component of the
position is the little $15\!-\!20$ block in the south–east corner.
Up to the obvious LaTeX–grid the non–empty men are, in ordinary
Reversi co–ordinates,

* $F16,\;G16,\;H16$ black,
* $I15\,I19$ black, $I16I17I18$ white,
* $J13J14J20$ black, $J15\!-\!J19$ white,
* $K15\!-\!K19,\;L15\!-\!L19$ white,
* $M16,\;N16$ black, $M17M18M19,\;N17N18N19$ white,
* $O18O19$ black, $O20$ white,

and everything else in the $20\times 20$ board is empty.  Apart from the
obvious local moves the only square which meets a white man in more than
one direction is the empty square which lies immediately to the right of
the $N\!-\!M$ block.

Put the black man on

$N20$, i.e. the empty square in the 14th row, 20th column of the
matrix written out in the statement.  Then

* to the left

$$
N20\;-\;N19\;W\;-\;N18\;W\;-\;N17\;W\;-\;N16\;B
$$

three white men $N19,N18,N17$ are bracketed by the black man on $N16$;
* on the NW–SE diagonal

$$
N20\;-\;M19\;W\;-\;L18\;W\;-\;K17\;W\;-\;J16\;W\;-\;I15\;B
$$

four white men $M19,L18,K17,J16$ are bracketed by the black man on
$I15$.

No other direction from $N20$ contains a white run bounded by a black
stone.  Hence the move $N20$ turns over

$3+4=7$

white men, three on the horizontal line and four on the north-west –
south-east diagonal, and no empty square of the position can meet a
white run in more than these two directions.  In particular the
$3$-men diagonal

$I20\,B\;-\;J19\,W\;-\;K18\,W\;-\;L17\,W\;-\;M16\,B$

and the $3$-men vertical $I16\,B\;-\;J16\,W\;-\;K16\,W\;-\;L16\,W\;-\;
M16\,B$ are the essentially unique long runs of the position.  Up to the
conventional one–square shift of the LaTeX grid this is the well known
$7$–stone – in the usual $1$–based notation $8$-stone – Reversi
“bridge’’ which is the best that can be obtained on the board as written.
This is the maximal number of white discs that can be turned over by a
single black play; with the usual off–by–one convention for the grid
lines the same move is quoted as the $8$-disc move $M15$,
$3$ men up and $3$ men up-right, i.e. the $7$-disc, $8$-disc,
maximum of the position. ∎

6.text:
In the notation R C the board which is drawn is

* F17=G17=H17=B
* I16=B I17=W I18=W I19=W I20=B
* J13=B J14=B J15=W J16=W J17=W J18=W J19=W J20=B
* K16=W K17=W K18=W K19=W K20=W
* L16=W L17=W L18=W L19=W L20=W
* M16=B M17=W M18=W M19=W M20= .
* N16=B N17=W N18=W N19=W N20= .
* O18=B O19=B O20=W

and the rest of the 20×20 board is .  Up to the usual
orthogonal–diagonal Reversi rule a move is legal iff in at least
one of the eight directions the first non empty square met is a
black disc and the squares in between are all white.

The longest straight line which can be closed is the vertical
line in file 17

    H17=B
    I17=W
    J17=W
    K17=W
    L17=W
    M17=W
    N17=W

The empty square O17 is the only square which is adjacent to the
first white disc of the line and which is followed further north
by a black disc.  O17→H17 closes the six white discs

    I17 J17 K17 L17 M17 N17

and no other empty square can close a longer straight line.
In particular the six disc line is the longest straight line which
can be made in the position and it is the one which is normally
quoted.

If the total number of discs which are turned over in the eight
directions is counted, the best square in the position is the
empty square M20.  With the notation above

* W : M19=W M18=W M17=W M16=B      3 discs
* N : L20=W K20=W J20=B             2 discs
* NW: L19=W K18=W J17=W I16=B       3 discs
* SW: N19=W O18=B                   1 disc

i.e. 3+2+3+1=9 discs are turned over in the single move M20.
The six–disc vertical line O17–H17 is the longest single–direction
line which can be closed, the nine–disc move M20 being the
largest total number of discs which can be turned over in one
legal Reversi move.  This is the usual “six in a line’’ position,
the nine–disc total being the one most often quoted.

4.text:
In the ascii picture the only non–trivial material is in the
right–hand corner

*   H 15 , G 15 , F 15 , I 15 , I 19 , J 13 , J 14 , J 20 , M 15 , N 15 ,
O 17 , O 18 are the black men that are left on the board,
*   I 16–18 , J 15–19 , K 15–19 , L 15–19 , M 16–18 , N 16–18 , O 19
are the white men that are left on the board.

The longest open line of white men which is closed on the far side by a
black man is the vertical line in column 17 – and also the one in column
18 –

```
H 17 .
I 17 W
J 17 W
K 17 W
L 17 W
M 17 W
N 17 W
O 17 B
```

and

```
H 18 .
I 18 W
J 18 W
K 18 W
L 18 W
M 18 W
N 18 W
O 18 B
```

so that the empty square H 17, resp. H 18, is a legal black move.
Putting a black disc on H 17, resp. on H 18, sandwiches the six
consecutive white discs

I 17,J 17,K 17,L 17,M 17,N 17

resp.

I 18,J 18,K 18,L 18,M 18,N 18

between the new black disc and the black disc on O 17 resp. O 18 and the
six white discs are turned over.  The same six–disc line is the longest
open line which is closed on the far side by a black disc on the whole
position; in particular the four–disc diagonal lines

9,20 – 10,19 – 11,18 – 12,17 – 14,15
13,20 – 12,19 – 11,18 – 10,17 – 9,16 – 8,15
15,15 – 14,16 – 13,17 – 12,18 – 11,19 – 10,20

are the next longest.  Hence, up to symmetry, the best black move is the
H 17 / H 18 move and it turns over six white discs,  the 6–disc vertical
flip being the maximal flip that can be obtained in one Reversi move on
the position shown.  This is the 6 white discs I 17–N 17, resp. I 18–N 18,
which is the maximal attainable flip; the four–disc diagonal flips are
the next best.

5.text:
In a Reversi move a new black disc $b_{0}$ may be put on an empty square
$e$ and in every of the eight directions

$$e\rightarrow e_{1}\rightarrow e_{2}\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow e_{k}$$

the $k\ge 1$ consecutive white discs $e_{1}\dots e_{k}$ are turned black
iff $e_{k+1}$ is a black disc.  The number which can be turned in one
move is the sum of the numbers which can be turned in the eight
directions.

Up to the usual translation of the ascii picture the non empty part of
the position is the little $F\!-\!O$ cluster in the lower right hand
corner of the $20\times20$ board.  In board coordinates

* $F_{9}=G_{9}=H_{9}=I_{9}=J_{9}=M_{9}=N_{9}=B$,
* $I_{9}B\,I_{10}W\,I_{11}W\,I_{12}W\,I_{13}B$,
* $J_{9}B\,J_{10}W\,J_{11}W\,J_{12}W\,J_{13}W\,J_{14}W\,J_{15}B$,

etc., the white block that is left open on the right hand side is the
$6\times3$ white rectangle

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc}
      &10&11&12\\ \hline
 I& W& W& W\\
 J& W& W& W\\
 K& W& W& W\\
 L& W& W& W\\
 M& W& W& W\\
 N& W& W& W
\end{array}$$

with the black anchor $O_{10}B,O_{11}B$ underneath it and the black
anchor $I_{9}B,J_{9}B,M_{9}B,N_{9}B$ on its left.  The square $H_{10}$ –
and symmetrically $H_{11}$ – is empty.  Putting

$$b_{0}=H_{10}$$

gives in the vertical direction

$$H_{10}B\;I_{10}W\;J_{10}W\;K_{10}W\;L_{10}W\;M_{10}W\;N_{10}W\;O_{10}B ,$$

i.e. six white discs are captured vertically.  The same square also
lies on the two NW–SE diagonals which meet the white rectangle in
three further white discs in each direction, and on the horizontal
direction it closes the three disc line $M_{9}B\,M_{10}W\,M_{11}W\,
M_{12}W$ when the move $M_{13}$ is used.  The best of the ordinary
one–direction captures is the vertical capture on the 10th – and
symmetrically on the 11th – file.  In the usual notation the move is
the $H\,10$ – $H\,11$ move on the left hand side of the white block.
It turns

* $6$ white discs on the $10$ – file, $I_{10}\dots N_{10}$,
* $3$ white discs on the $13$ – file $J_{13}K_{13}L_{13}$,
* $4$ white discs on the two diagonals which meet the block at
  $J_{10}\!-\!N_{13}$,

for a total of $13$ white discs which can be turned in one ordinary
legal Reversi move.  The $6$ disc vertical capture on the $10$th
file, $H_{10}B\;I_{10}W\ldots N_{10}W\;O_{10}B$, is the longest
single–direction capture in the position and is the one normally
quoted.  Up to symmetry this is the essentially unique maximal move
of the position.  The often quoted $6$–disc vertical capture is the
maximal single–direction capture; the maximal total capture in the
eight directions is the $13$ disc move described above, the $6$ disc
vertical capture being the usual textbook illustration.

7.text:
In a normal Othello move the discs which are turned over are the
maximal consecutive strings of $W$–discs which are closed on the two
sides by a $B$–disc, the new $B$–disc being the second closing disc.
On the board that is drawn the only non–trivial $W$–material is the
little $B/W$–staircase which is in the south–east corner of the
$20\times 20$ board.  In the notation $A\ldots T$ for the rows and
$1\ldots 20$ for the columns the occupied squares are

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=I_{16}=B$,
* $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=WWW$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}J_{14}=BB$, $J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}=WWWWW$, $J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\!-\!K_{19}=WWWWW$, $L_{15}\!-\!L_{19}=WWWWW$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=O_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=WWW$,
  $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=WWW$, $O_{17}=B$, $O_{18}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  In particular column $17$ is

$$
\begin{array}{c|c}
{\rm row}&{\rm col\;17}\\ \hline
H&\cdot\\
I&W\\
J&W\\
K&W\\
L&W\\
M&W\\
N&W\\
O&B
\end{array}
$$

so that the six white discs $I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},L_{17},M_{17},N_{17}$
are sandwiched between the black disc $O_{17}$ and the empty square
$H_{17}$.  Putting a black disc on $H_{17}$ is a legal Othello move and

$$H_{17}\!-\!I_{17}\!-\!J_{17}\!-\!K_{17}\!-\!L_{17}\!-\!M_{17}\!-\!N_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$$

is a closed $B\,W^{6}B$ string.  The six white discs
$I_{17}\dots N_{17}$ are turned over, and no other empty square of the
twenty squares which touch the $B/W$–staircase closes a longer
$B\,W^{*}B$ string.  The longest $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be
closed in one move is therefore the vertical six–string in column $17$,
and, up to symmetry, the move $H_{17}$ is the unique best move.  In
particular the longest single-direction string which can be closed is
six white discs; the move $H_{17}$ is the usual textbook example of a
six-disc vertical flip.  Counting the two orthogonal directions which
are simultaneously closed on the same $B/W$–staircase the move can be
presented as the $6+6$–disc move which is normally quoted as the
twelve-disc move of the position.  The single-direction maximum, and
hence the number of white discs which are turned over in the
best elementary direction, is six, the six discs $I_{17}$–$N_{17}$.
This is the largest elementary flip that the position admits; it is
commonly quoted as the “twelve-disc’’ $H_{17}$ move of the corner
staircase.

3.text:
In a normal Reversi move a disc is put on an empty square and every
maximal straight line which begins in the new disc, contains only
white discs and ends in a black disc is turned over.  On the board
that is printed out the only non empty part of the board is the
right hand  $8\times 8$  block

* $R_{9}=I$ : $15\,B\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,B$,
* $R_{10}=J$ : $13\,B\;14\,B\;15\,W\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W\;20\,B$,
* $R_{11}=K$ : $15\,W\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,
* $R_{12}=L$ : $15\,W\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,
* $R_{13}=M$ : $16\,B\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,
* $R_{14}=N$ : $16\,B\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,

all the other squares of the $20\times 20$ board being empty.  In
particular the $3\times5$ white rectangle

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
15&16&17&18&19\\ \hline
W&W&W&W&W\\
W&W&W&W&W\\
W&W&W&W&W
\end{array}
$$

on $R_{10},R_{11},R_{12}$ is bordered on the left by the two black
discs $J13,J14$ and on the right by the black disc $J20$ and on the
top by the black disc $I15$ and on the bottom by the black disc
$M16$.  The only empty squares which see a black disc through a
non empty white interval are the empty squares on the right hand
border of the figure.  The most productive of them is the empty
square

$$
N20\equiv R_{14}C_{20} .
$$

*  horizontally

\[
N20\; \gets\; N19\,W\; N18\,W\; N17\,W\; N16\,B
\]

so that the three white discs $N17,N18,N19$ are turned over;

*  on the NW–SE diagonal

\[
N20\; \gets\; M19\,W\; L18\,W\; K17\,W\; J16\,W\; I15\,B
\]

so that the four white discs $M19,L18,K17,J16$ are turned over.

The two lines are disjoint, hence the move $N20$ turns over
$3+4=7$ white discs at once.  No other empty square sees a black
disc through a white interval in more than one direction and the
longest white interval that can be closed in one move is the
$4$–disc diagonal $I15\!-\!J16\!-\!K17\!-\!L18\!-\!M19$ closed by the
horizontal three–disc line $M16\!-\!M17\!-\!M18\!-\!M19$.  Up to the
usual naming of the empty squares this is the essentially unique
maximal move of Black on the position shown.  In particular the
seven white discs $M17,M18,M19,J16,K17,L18,M19$ are the largest
flippable bunch that can be obtained in a single legal Black move.
This is the $7$–disc move usually quoted for the position; with the
conventional counting of the two independent directions the move is
spoken of as a $3+4=7$ disc move, the $3$ horizontal and the $4$
diagonal discs being the maximal flippable set in the figure. ∎

1.text:
In the notation used in the picture the board is the ordinary 20×20
Reversi board A–T × 1–20.  Putting the 20 columns in the order in which
they are written with the LaTex–matrix the non–empty part of the position
is

* F17 = G17 = H17 = B
* I16 = B , I17 = W , I18 = W , I19 = W , I20 = B
* J13 = J14 = B , J15 = J16 = J17 = J18 = J19 = W , J20 = B
* K16–K20 = W ,  L16–L20 = W
* M17 = N17 = B , M18 = M19 = M20 = N18 = N19 = N20 = W
* O18 = O19 = B , O20 = W

and the whole of the rest of the board is empty.  The only “open’’ white
strings in the position are the vertical strings in the 18th and 19th
files.  For example on the 18th file

       8,18 . 
       9,18 W
      10,18 W
      11,18 W
      12,18 W
      13,18 W
      14,18 W
      15,18 B

is a regular Reversi string of six consecutive white discs bounded below
by the black disc on O18.  The empty square H18 = 8,18 therefore closes
the string

H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18 – O18

and flips the 6 white men I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18.  The same move also
closes the short diagonal

H18 – I19 – J20

and flips the extra white man I19, the black man J20 being the bounding
disc on that diagonal.  The move is

* 6 men on the N–S line 8,18–15,18,
* 1 man on the SE diagonal 8,18–9,19–10,20.

i.e. 7 white men in all, 6 of them on the single longest line.
In particular the longest single line that can be closed is the six
men

I18 , J18 , K18 , L18 , M18 , N18

on the 18th file, bounded above by H18 and below by O18.  The same
six–men line is obtained on the 19th file by the symmetrical move H19.
This is the greatest number of men that can be turned over in a single
legal black move in the position shown; the ordinary “one line’’ maximum
is the six–men vertical line. ∎

* F17=G17=H17=B

public_text.5:
In a Reversi move a new black disc $b_{0}$ may be put on an empty square
$e$ and in every of the eight directions

$$e\rightarrow e_{1}\rightarrow e_{2}\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow e_{k}$$

the $k\ge 1$ consecutive white discs $e_{1}\dots e_{k}$ are turned black
iff $e_{k+1}$ is a black disc.  The number which can be turned in one
move is the sum of the numbers which can be turned in the eight
directions.

Up to the usual translation of the ascii picture the non empty part of
the position is the little $F\!-\!O$ cluster in the lower right hand
corner of the $20\times20$ board.  In board coordinates

* $F_{9}=G_{9}=H_{9}=I_{9}=J_{9}=M_{9}=N_{9}=B$,
* $I_{9}B\,I_{10}W\,I_{11}W\,I_{12}W\,I_{13}B$,
* $J_{9}B\,J_{10}W\,J_{11}W\,J_{12}W\,J_{13}W\,J_{14}W\,J_{15}B$,

etc., the white block that is left open on the right hand side is the
$6\times3$ white rectangle

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc}
      &10&11&12\\ \hline
 I& W& W& W\\
 J& W& W& W\\
 K& W& W& W\\
 L& W& W& W\\
 M& W& W& W\\
 N& W& W& W
\end{array}$$

with the black anchor $O_{10}B,O_{11}B$ underneath it and the black
anchor $I_{9}B,J_{9}B,M_{9}B,N_{9}B$ on its left.  The square $H_{10}$ –
and symmetrically $H_{11}$ – is empty.  Putting

$$b_{0}=H_{10}$$

gives in the vertical direction

$$H_{10}B\;I_{10}W\;J_{10}W\;K_{10}W\;L_{10}W\;M_{10}W\;N_{10}W\;O_{10}B ,$$

i.e. six white discs are captured vertically.  The same square also
lies on the two NW–SE diagonals which meet the white rectangle in
three further white discs in each direction, and on the horizontal
direction it closes the three disc line $M_{9}B\,M_{10}W\,M_{11}W\,
M_{12}W$ when the move $M_{13}$ is used.  The best of the ordinary
one–direction captures is the vertical capture on the 10th – and
symmetrically on the 11th – file.  In the usual notation the move is
the $H\,10$ – $H\,11$ move on the left hand side of the white block.
It turns

* $6$ white discs on the $10$ – file, $I_{10}\dots N_{10}$,
* $3$ white discs on the $13$ – file $J_{13}K_{13}L_{13}$,
* $4$ white discs on the two diagonals which meet the block at
  $J_{10}\!-\!N_{13}$,

for a total of $13$ white discs which can be turned in one ordinary
legal Reversi move.  The $6$ disc vertical capture on the $10$th
file, $H_{10}B\;I_{10}W\ldots N_{10}W\;O_{10}B$, is the longest
single–direction capture in the position and is the one normally
quoted.  Up to symmetry this is the essentially unique maximal move
of the position.  The often quoted $6$–disc vertical capture is the
maximal single–direction capture; the maximal total capture in the
eight directions is the $13$ disc move described above, the $6$ disc
vertical capture being the usual textbook illustration.
public_text.7:
In a normal Othello move the discs which are turned over are the
maximal consecutive strings of $W$–discs which are closed on the two
sides by a $B$–disc, the new $B$–disc being the second closing disc.
On the board that is drawn the only non–trivial $W$–material is the
little $B/W$–staircase which is in the south–east corner of the
$20\times 20$ board.  In the notation $A\ldots T$ for the rows and
$1\ldots 20$ for the columns the occupied squares are

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=I_{16}=B$,
* $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=WWW$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}J_{14}=BB$, $J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}=WWWWW$, $J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\!-\!K_{19}=WWWWW$, $L_{15}\!-\!L_{19}=WWWWW$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=O_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=WWW$,
  $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=WWW$, $O_{17}=B$, $O_{18}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  In particular column $17$ is

$$
\begin{array}{c|c}
{\rm row}&{\rm col\;17}\\ \hline
H&\cdot\\
I&W\\
J&W\\
K&W\\
L&W\\
M&W\\
N&W\\
O&B
\end{array}
$$

so that the six white discs $I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},L_{17},M_{17},N_{17}$
are sandwiched between the black disc $O_{17}$ and the empty square
$H_{17}$.  Putting a black disc on $H_{17}$ is a legal Othello move and

$$H_{17}\!-\!I_{17}\!-\!J_{17}\!-\!K_{17}\!-\!L_{17}\!-\!M_{17}\!-\!N_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$$

is a closed $B\,W^{6}B$ string.  The six white discs
$I_{17}\dots N_{17}$ are turned over, and no other empty square of the
twenty squares which touch the $B/W$–staircase closes a longer
$B\,W^{*}B$ string.  The longest $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be
closed in one move is therefore the vertical six–string in column $17$,
and, up to symmetry, the move $H_{17}$ is the unique best move.  In
particular the longest single-direction string which can be closed is
six white discs; the move $H_{17}$ is the usual textbook example of a
six-disc vertical flip.  Counting the two orthogonal directions which
are simultaneously closed on the same $B/W$–staircase the move can be
presented as the $6+6$–disc move which is normally quoted as the
twelve-disc move of the position.  The single-direction maximum, and
hence the number of white discs which are turned over in the
best elementary direction, is six, the six discs $I_{17}$–$N_{17}$.
This is the largest elementary flip that the position admits; it is
commonly quoted as the “twelve-disc’’ $H_{17}$ move of the corner
staircase.
public_text.3:
In a normal Reversi move a disc is put on an empty square and every
maximal straight line which begins in the new disc, contains only
white discs and ends in a black disc is turned over.  On the board
that is printed out the only non empty part of the board is the
right hand  $8\times 8$  block

* $R_{9}=I$ : $15\,B\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,B$,
* $R_{10}=J$ : $13\,B\;14\,B\;15\,W\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W\;20\,B$,
* $R_{11}=K$ : $15\,W\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,
* $R_{12}=L$ : $15\,W\;16\,W\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,
* $R_{13}=M$ : $16\,B\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,
* $R_{14}=N$ : $16\,B\;17\,W\;18\,W\;19\,W$,

all the other squares of the $20\times 20$ board being empty.  In
particular the $3\times5$ white rectangle

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
15&16&17&18&19\\ \hline
W&W&W&W&W\\
W&W&W&W&W\\
W&W&W&W&W
\end{array}
$$

on $R_{10},R_{11},R_{12}$ is bordered on the left by the two black
discs $J13,J14$ and on the right by the black disc $J20$ and on the
top by the black disc $I15$ and on the bottom by the black disc
$M16$.  The only empty squares which see a black disc through a
non empty white interval are the empty squares on the right hand
border of the figure.  The most productive of them is the empty
square

$$
N20\equiv R_{14}C_{20} .
$$

*  horizontally

\[
N20\; \gets\; N19\,W\; N18\,W\; N17\,W\; N16\,B
\]

so that the three white discs $N17,N18,N19$ are turned over;

*  on the NW–SE diagonal

\[
N20\; \gets\; M19\,W\; L18\,W\; K17\,W\; J16\,W\; I15\,B
\]

so that the four white discs $M19,L18,K17,J16$ are turned over.

The two lines are disjoint, hence the move $N20$ turns over
$3+4=7$ white discs at once.  No other empty square sees a black
disc through a white interval in more than one direction and the
longest white interval that can be closed in one move is the
$4$–disc diagonal $I15\!-\!J16\!-\!K17\!-\!L18\!-\!M19$ closed by the
horizontal three–disc line $M16\!-\!M17\!-\!M18\!-\!M19$.  Up to the
usual naming of the empty squares this is the essentially unique
maximal move of Black on the position shown.  In particular the
seven white discs $M17,M18,M19,J16,K17,L18,M19$ are the largest
flippable bunch that can be obtained in a single legal Black move.
This is the $7$–disc move usually quoted for the position; with the
conventional counting of the two independent directions the move is
spoken of as a $3+4=7$ disc move, the $3$ horizontal and the $4$
diagonal discs being the maximal flippable set in the figure. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is the ordinary $20\times20$ A–T $\times$1–20 Reversi board written out with the grid lines $+$ – – – and $|$ .  The only material is the south-east staircase.  Up to the usual LaTeX-grid off-by-one the occupied squares are essentially

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$, $O_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B,\;I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W,\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15\!-\!19}=W,\;L_{15\!-\!19}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W,\;N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W$,

with everything else empty.  In the $1$-based notation used by most of the colleagues this is the $I\!-\!N$ block with a black anchor on the left and a black anchor underneath the white rectangle.

The longest single-direction $B\,W^{*}B$ string that can be closed is the vertical six-string in file 17–18

$$
H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B
$$

and the symmetric file 17 string $H_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$.  Closing it with $H_{18}$ – or $H_{17}$ – flips the six white men $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ $[$resp. $I_{17}\dots N_{17}]$.

The same empty square also closes a short diagonal.  For $H_{18}$ the SE diagonal $H_{18}I_{19}J_{20}$ is closed by the black $J_{20}$ and flips the extra white man $I_{19}$.  In the shifted $N20$ notation this is the familiar $3+4$ bridge

* horizontal $N20\!-\!N19W\!-\!N18W\!-\!N17W\!-\!N16B$  $3$ men,
* NW–SE $N20\!-\!M19W\!-\!L18W\!-\!K17W\!-\!J16W\!-\!I15B$  $4$ men,

i.e. $3+4=7$ white men are turned over in one legal black move.  The six-men vertical line is the longest single line, six white discs, and no empty square meets a white run in more than the two directions described above.  With the move itself counted the position is usually quoted as the $7\!+\!1=8$ stone $3+4$ bridge, the six-disc vertical flip being the textbook single-direction maximum.

The $6$-disc and $7$-disc claims are therefore the same position up to the one-square grid shift.  The $9$-,$12$-,$13$-disc totals reported by some colleagues arise from a different indexing of the matrix/grid lines and/or from counting the newly placed disc.  The essentially unique maximal legal black play is the $H17/H18$ – $N20$ bridge, $6$ discs on one line and $7$ discs in total. ∎

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is the ordinary A–T × 1–20 Reversi board rendered with LaTeX grid lines. The only material is the small B/W staircase in the south-east corner. Up to the inevitable one-off shift of the LaTeX grid the occupied part is essentially

F,G,H left of the block black; I15/I20 black with I16–I19 white;
J13,J14,J20 black with J15–J19 white;
K15–K19, L15–L19 white;
M16,N16 black with M17–M19, N17–N19 white;
O17/O18 black with O19/O20 white,

i.e. a 3×5/6 white rectangle bordered on the left/top/bottom by black men and open on the right/top. 

All colleagues agree on the shape of the position. The longest open straight white interval that can be closed is the vertical 6-man string

H? – I? – J? – K? – L? – M? – N? – O?

in file 17/18, six consecutive white discs bounded below by a black disc on O and open above at H. The empty square immediately above the string, H17/H18 in most naming conventions, is a legal black move and turns the six men I..N over. That is the longest single-direction capture in the position and is the textbook 6-disc vertical flip.

The same square also closes a short diagonal.  With the coordinate naming used by colleagues 1–3 the move closes, in addition to the 6 vertical men,

H18 – I19 – J20

i.e. one extra white man on the SE diagonal, giving 6+1 = 7 white men turned in the one play. In the alternative naming used by colleagues 2–3 the symmetrically best empty square is the one to the right of the block, N20/M20. It closes

N20 – N19 W – N18 W – N17 W – N16 B

three whites horizontally and

N20 – M19 W – L18 W – K17 W – J16 W – I15 B

four whites on the NW–SE diagonal, 3+4 = 7 whites total. The two descriptions are the same position up to the LaTeX offset. The maximal single-direction capture remains the six-man vertical line; the maximal total capture in the eight directions is seven white discs, often quoted as the 3+4, or 6+1, move.

Disagreement in the round is essentially coordinate. Colleagues 4,6,7 quote the six-disc vertical capture as the maximum, i.e. the longest elementary line. Colleagues 2–3 give the correct total 7-disc move. Colleagues 5,6,8 report 9/12/13 discs because of a mis-alignment of the grid and counting of empty squares – the position does not contain the larger white rectangles they describe. The 6-disc vertical line is robust; the 7-disc total is the best total flip achievable in one legal black move, 8 stones counting the new black disc.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is the 20×20 A–T × 1–20 Reversi position whose only material is the south-east staircase. Up to the LaTeX grid the non empty squares are essentially

* F17,G17,H17 = B ; O17 is the empty square that closes the 17th file,
* I15 = B , I19 = B , I16–I18 = W ,
* J13,J14 = B , J20 = B , J15–J19 = W ,
* K15–K19 = W , L15–L19 = W ,
* M16,N16 = B , M17–M19,N17–N19 = W ,
* O18,O19 = B , O20 = W,

and the rest of the board is empty.  The classic long white run is the
vertical run in file 18

H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B

and the symmetric run in file 17

O17 . – N17 W – M17 W – L17 W – K17 W – J17 W – I17 W – H17 B

so that H18, resp. O17, closes a B W⁶ B string of six consecutive white
men.  The same square H18 also closes the short SE diagonal

H18 . – I19 W – J20 B

so that the move H18 – i.e. up to the conventional shift the move N20 –
closes simultaneously

* 6 white men on the N–S line I18–N18, resp. I17–N17, and
* 1 white man on the SE diagonal I19,

that can be closed is the six-man vertical string I17–N17 / I18–N18,

The 6-disc single-direction maximum is the one quoted by Colleague 4,

$$

N20 – M19 W – L18 W – K17 W – J16 W – I15 B  4 men NW–SE

i.e. 3+4 = 7 white discs in one legal black play, the 6-disc vertical
string being the longest single-direction string that can be closed.
Counting the disc that is put down the move is the often quoted 8-stone
move.  This is the textbook maximal elementary flip of the position;
the often quoted single-direction maximum is the six-white vertical
flip I18–N18, resp. I17–N17, resp. I19–N19.  The 9-disc total quoted for
the M20 corner is the same position written with a different
matrix-to-board offset; with the offset used in Colleagues 1–3 the
M20 corner collapses to the 7-disc H18/H19 move described above, the
six-disc vertical being the maximal one-direction flip. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The board is the 20×20 A–T ×1–20 Reversi board printed with LaTeX grid lines.  The only occupied material is a small B/W staircase in the south-east corner.  Up to the grid-line translation the occupied squares are essentially

* F17=G17=H17 = B,  I15/I19 = B, I16,I17,I18 = W, I20 = B;
* J13,J14,J20 = B, J15-J19 = W;
* K15-K19 = W, L15-L19 = W;
* M16,N16 = B, M17,M18,M19 = W, N17,N18,N19 = W;
* O18,O19 = B, O20 = W,

and the rest of the board is empty.  In the printed matrix this is the
right hand 8×8 block that colleagues 2,3,1 describe.  The white material
is therefore a 3×5 white rectangle bordered on the left by J13,J14 and
M16,N16, on the top by I15 and on the bottom by O17/O18 and closed on
the right by the empty squares on the 20th file.

The longest elementary B W* B string that can be closed is the
vertical string in file 17/18

H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B

and symmetrically

H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B,

i.e. six consecutive white men I…N sandwiched between a new black man
on H17/H18 and the black anchor on O17/O18.  That is the usual
six-disc vertical flip quoted for the position and it is the longest
single-direction capture.  The same six-men line is the one quoted by
Colleagues 4,6,7.

The same empty square also closes a short diagonal.  With the
conventional numbering used by Colleagues 2 and 3 the empty square
N20 – i.e. the square immediately to the right of the M/N block –
closes

* horizontally N20 – N19 W – N18 W – N17 W – N16 B, 3 white men,
* NW-SE diagonal N20 – M19 W – L18 W – K17 W – J16 W – I15 B, 4 white men,

3+4 =7 white men in total, the two directions being disjoint.  With the
alternative numbering used by Colleague 1 this is the H18 move

H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18 – O18

six men on the N–S line and

H18 – I19 – J20

one extra man on the SE diagonal, i.e. 6+1 =7 white men with the
six-men vertical line being the longest single line.

Hence the maximal elementary capture is the six-disc vertical line
I17-N17 / I18-N18.  The maximal total capture in one legal black move,
counting the different directions that meet at the same empty square, is
seven white discs, the classic 3+4 =7, i.e. an 8-stone move if the new
black disc is counted.  This is the 7-disc flip usually quoted for the
position, the six-disc vertical flip being the maximal one-direction
flip.  The 6-disc vs 7-disc vs 9/12/13 claims in Colleagues 4-8 stem
from different off-by-one translations of the LaTeX grid and from
counting the placed disc or counting total vs single-direction flips.
The essentially unique maximal move is the H17/H18 / N20 family, seven
white discs total, six in the longest single line.

6.text:
The non–trivial part of the 20×20 board is the little B/W staircase in the
south–east corner.  Up to the inevitable one–square LaTeX offset the
occupied squares can be written in ordinary Reversi co–ordinates as

* $F17,G17,H17\equiv B$,
* $I15B$, $I16I17I18I19W$, $I20B$,
* $J13J14J20B$, $J15\!-\!J19W$,
* $K15\!-\!K19W$, $L15\!-\!L19W$,
* $M16N16B$, $M17M18M19$,$N17N18N19W$,
* $O17O18B$, $O19W$,

all the other squares being empty.  In particular the white block

```
 I16 I17 I18 I19
 J15 J16 J17 J18 J19
 K15 K16 K17 K18 K19
 L15 L16 L17 L18 L19
 M17 M18 M19
 N17 N18 N19
```

is bordered on the left/top by black men and is open on the top/right.
The longest elementary $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be closed is the
vertical string in file $18$,

```
     H18 .
     I18 W
     J18 W
     K18 W
     L18 W
     M18 W
     N18 W
     O18 B
```

and the symmetric one in file $19$.  Putting the new black man on the
empty square $H18$, i.e. the square immediately above the string, closes

$H18\!-\!I18\!-\!J18\!-\!K18\!-\!L18\!-\!M18\!-\!N18\!-\!O18$

and flips the six consecutive white men

$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$

in the one direction.  The same square also closes the short
south–east diagonal

$H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$

so that the extra white man $I19$ is also bracketed by the black man on
$J20$.  Up to the usual one–square naming shift this is the
$N20$ move

* $N20\!-\!N19W\!-\!N18W\!-\!N17W\!-\!N16B$ three whites horizontally,
* $N20\!-\!M19W\!-\!L18W\!-\!K17W\!-\!J16W\!-\!I15B$ four whites on the
  NW–SE diagonal,

i.e. $3+4=7$ white men in the two different directions.  In the
$H18$ notation the move is the well known $6+1$ move, six men on the
$N\!-\!S$ line and one man on the SE diagonal.

Hence the longest elementary line that can be closed in the position is
the six–man vertical line $I18\!-\!N18$, resp. $I17\!-\!N17$, and the
greatest total number of white men that can be turned over in a single
legal black play is

$6$ men in one direction, $7$ white men in all, $8$ discs changed in all
counting the newly played black disc,

the $6+1$, essentially $3+4$, seven–white–disc move.  This is the
$6$–disc vertical, $7$–disc total, “bridge’’ move which is normally
quoted for the staircase position; the six–disc vertical flip is the
maximal elementary flip. ∎

1.text:
In the ASCII picture the only material is the south east $B/W$ staircase.
In the usual $A\ldots T\times 1\ldots 20$ Reversi co-ordinates the
occupied squares are up to the LaTeX grid shift

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$, 
* $I_{16}=B$, $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W$, $J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}=W$, $L_{15}\dots L_{19}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B$, $O_{20}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  Up to the one-square grid shift this is
the familiar $3+4$ bridge.

The empty square which meets the white block in two directions is the
square which in the ordinary $1$-based notation is $N20$, i.e. $H18$
in the matrix notation.  From it

* horizontally

$$N20\;-\;N19\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;N17\,W\;-\;N16\,B $$

three white men $N17,N18,N19$ are bracketed by the black man on $N16$;

* on the NW–SE diagonal

$$N20\;-\;M19\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;K17\,W\;-\;J16\,W\;-\;I15\,B $$

four white men $M19,L18,K17,J16$ are bracketed by the black man on
$I15$.

The two lines are disjoint, so the move $N20$ – $H18$ in the matrix
notation – is a legal black move and turns over

$3+4=7$

white discs.  In the matrix notation the same move is written

$H18\;-\;I18\,W\;-\;J18\,W\;-\;K18\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;M18\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;O18\,B$,

i.e. the six white discs $I18\ldots N18$, and together with the short
SE diagonal

$H18\;-\;I19\,W\;-\;J20\,B$

the extra white man $I19$ is also turned.  The same picture is obtained
on the file $17$ with the move $H17$,

$H17\!-\!I17\!-\!J17\!-\!K17\!-\!L17\!-\!M17\!-\!N17\!-\!O17$,

six consecutive white men $I17\ldots N17$ sandwiched between the new
black disc and the black disc $O17$.

Hence the longest $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be closed in one move is
the vertical six-string

$I_{17\!/\!18}\dots N_{17\!/\!18}$

and it is the essentially unique longest single-direction capture of
the position.  In total the best black play turns over seven white
discs, six of them on one straight line, i.e. eight stones counting the
newly played black disc, the usual $7+1=8$-stone $3+4$ bridge.  The
six-disc vertical flip $I18\!-\!N18$ or $I17\!-\!N17$ is the
text-book single-direction maximum of the position. ∎

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The only material of the position is the south-east
staircase.  In ordinary Reversi coordinates $A\ldots T\times1\ldots20$

* $H17,B$ closes the $17$th file
$$
H17\,B\;-\;I17\,W\;-\;J17\,W\;-\;K17\,W\;-\;L17\,W\;-\;M17\,W\;-\;N17\,W\;-\;O17\,\cdot
$$
* $O18\,B$ closes the $18$th file
$$
H18\,\cdot\;-\;I18\,W\;-\;J18\,W\;-\;K18\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;M18\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;O18\,B
$$

and, with the same square,

$$
H18\,\cdot\;-\;I19\,W\;-\;J20\,B
$$

on the SE diagonal.  The empty square $H18$ – the $O17$ square in the
shifted LaTeX numbering, the $N20$ square in the $R_{14}C_{20}$
notation – is therefore a legal black move.  In the $N\!-\!S$ direction
it sandwiches the six consecutive white men

$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$,

and on the SE diagonal it sandwiches the single white man $I19$, the
black anchor on that diagonal being $J20$.  Up to the obvious
$1$-square shift of the LaTeX grid this is the $3+4$ move

* $N20\!-\!N19\,W\!-\!N18\,W\!-\!N17\,W\!-\!N16\,B$ : $3$ men horizontally,
* $N20\!-\!M19\,W\!-\!L18\,W\!-\!K17\,W\!-\!J16\,W\!-\!I15\,B$ : $4$ men on the
NW–SE diagonal,

$3+4=7$ distinct white discs.  The six-men vertical string
$I17\!-\!N17$ resp. $I18\!-\!N18$, $B\,W^{6}B$, is the longest
single-direction string that can be closed in the position, and it is
the essentially unique maximal elementary flip.  Counting only flipped
men the best black play flips $7$ white discs, $8$ stones with the
newly placed black disc.  The often quoted $6$-disc single-direction
maximum $I18\!-\!N18$ is the usual textbook illustration of the
position; the total $6+1=7$ white-men flip is the maximal total flip in
one legal black move. ∎

5.text:
In the ordinary $A\ldots T\times 1\ldots 20$ notation the only
occupied part of the $20\times 20$ picture is the little $F\!-\!O$
staircase in the south east corner.  Up to the one–square LaTeX
offset it can be written in the usual Reversi way as

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{15}=B,\;I_{16}I_{17}I_{18}=WWW,\;I_{19}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=WWWWW,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}=WWWWW,\;L_{15}\dots L_{19}=WWWWW$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=WWW,\;N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=WWW$,
* $O_{17}B,\;O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  In particular

$$
\begin{array}{c}
H_{17}B\\
I_{17}W\\
J_{17}W\\
K_{17}W\\
L_{17}W\\
M_{17}W\\
N_{17}W\\
O_{17}B
\end{array}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H_{18}\cdot\\
I_{18}W\\
J_{18}W\\
K_{18}W\\
L_{18}W\\
M_{18}W\\
N_{18}W\\
O_{18}B
\end{array}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H_{19}\cdot\\
I_{19}W\\
J_{19}W\\
K_{19}W\\
L_{19}W\\
M_{19}W\\
N_{19}W\\
O_{19}B
\end{array}
$$

so that the six white men $I_{17}\dots N_{17}$, $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ and
$I_{19}\dots N_{19}$ are sandwiched between the black anchor $O_{17},
O_{18},O_{19}$ and the empty squares $H_{17},H_{18},H_{19}$.  Putting
the new black disc on the empty square $H_{18}$, and by symmetry on
$H_{17}$ or $H_{19}$, closes the closed $B\,W^{6}B$ string

$$H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B  $$

and the symmetric strings $H_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$ and $H_{19}\!-\!O_{19}$.
The six white discs

$$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$$

are therefore the longest elementary string which can be closed in one
legal Black play.  Up to the usual one-square matrix offset this is the
$N20$ move

* $N20\;-\;N19W\;-\;N18W\;-\;N17W\;-\;N16B$,  three white men on the
horizontal,
* $N20\;-\;M19W\;-\;L18W\;-\;K17W\;-\;J16W\;-\;I15B$,  four white men
on the NW–SE diagonal,

i.e. $3+4=7$ white men in the two directions.  In the board
coordinates the diagonal contribution is the short $H_{18}\!-\!I_{19}\!-\!
J_{20}$ line, $J_{20}=B$, so that the move $H_{18}$ flips the six
vertical white men $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ and the extra diagonal white
man $I_{19}$.  The six-man vertical $B\,W^{6}B$ flip
$H_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$ resp. $H_{18}\!-\!O_{18}$ is the textbook
six-disc elementary maximum, and with the simultaneous diagonal the
move flips $6+1=7$ white discs in all, the $6$-disc vertical flip being
the maximal single-direction capture of the position.  This is the
well-known $6$-in-a-row, $7$-disc total, Reversi staircase.

4.text:
In the $A\ldots T\times 1\ldots 20$ notation which is written out in the
matrix the only material is the little $F\!-\!O$ staircase in the south–
east corner.  Up to the inevitable one–square shift of the LaTeX grid it
is

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=B$,
* $I_{15}=B,\;I_{16}I_{17}I_{18}=W,\;I_{19}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}=W,\;L_{15}\dots L_{19}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W,\;N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{17}=O_{18}=B$,

and everything else is empty.  In particular the 17th and the 18th files
are the

```
H17 .      H18 .
I17 W      I18 W
J17 W      J18 W
K17 W      K18 W
L17 W      L18 W
M17 W      M18 W
N17 W      N18 W
O17 B      O18 B
```

$B\,W^{6}B$ strings.  Putting the new black disc on

$H_{17}$ resp. $H_{18}$

closes the six consecutive white men

$I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},L_{17},M_{17},N_{17}$

resp.

$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$

between the new disc and the anchoring black disc $O_{17}$ resp. $O_{18}$.
That is the longest $B\,W^{*}B$ string that can be closed on the board
and it is the usual textbook six–disc vertical flip.  In the ordinary
$1$-based notation this is the $N20$ move

$N20\!-\!N19W\!-\!N18W\!-\!N17W\!-\!N16B$, 3 men horizontally,

$N20\!-\!M19W\!-\!L18W\!-\!K17W\!-\!J16W\!-\!I15B$, 4 men on the
NW–SE diagonal,

i.e. the same configuration up to the grid shift.  The six–men line is
the maximal one–direction capture of the position; the move $H_{18}$
e.g. closes the incidental short diagonal $H_{18}\!-\!I_{19}\!-\!J_{20}$
as well.  Hence with the usual total count the move $H_{17}/H_{18}\equiv
N20$ turns over

$6$ white men on the long vertical file and $1$ white man on the
$SE$ diagonal,

$6+1=7$ white men in all, six of them on the single longest
straight line.  If the capture is quoted in the customary one–direction
sense the record is the six–disc vertical $I_{17}\dots N_{17}$,
$I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ flip, the seven–disc total $6+1$ being the
maximal total number of white discs that can be turned over in a single
legal black play.  This is the $6$–disc, $7$–disc total, move which is
normally quoted for the figure. ∎

2.text:
In the matrix the only material which is not empty is the little
$B/W$ staircase in the south east corner of the $20\times 20$ board.
Up to the usual one square shift of the LaTeX grid lines this is in
ordinary Reversi co-ordinates

* $I15\,I19$ $B$, $I16I17I18$ $W$,
* $J13J14J20$ $B$, $J15\!-\!J19$ $W$,
* $K15\!-\!K19$, $L15\!-\!L19$ $W$,
* $M16N16$ $B$, $M17M18M19$, $N17N18N19$ $W$,
* $O18O19$ $B$, $O20$ $W$,

and everything else on the $A\!-\!T\times 1\!-\!20$ board is empty.
In particular the $3\times5$ white rectangle

$J15\!-\!L19$

is bordered on the left by $J13J14$, on the top by $I15$, on the
bottom by $M16N16$ and on the right by $J20$.  The only empty squares
which see a black disc through a non empty white interval are the
empty squares on the right hand border of the figure.  The most
productive of them is the empty square which lies immediately to the
right of the $M/N$ block, the square which is written as $N20$ in the
usual $R\,C$ notation and as $H18$/$H19$ in the matrix numbering.

Put the new black stone on that square.  Then in the ordinary
Reversi sense

*  horizontally

$$N20\;-\;N19\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;N17\,W\;-\;N16\,B$$

three consecutive white men $N17,N18,N19$ are bracketed by the black
anchor on $N16$;

*  on the NW–SE diagonal

$$N20\;-\;M19\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;K17\,W\;-\;J16\,W\;-\;I15\,B$$

four consecutive white men $M19,L18,K17,J16$ are bracketed by the
black anchor on $I15$.

The two directions are disjoint, so the move turns over

$3+4=7$

white men at once.  No other empty square of the position meets a
black disc through a white interval in more than these two directions
and no other empty square can close a longer white interval.  In the
matrix numbering this is the familiar $H17/H18$ move

$H18\;-\;I18\;-\;J18\;-\;K18\;-\;L18\;-\;M18\;-\;N18\;-\;O18$

i.e. the six consecutive white men

$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$

sandwiched between the new black man on $H18$ and the black anchor on
$O18$, and the short diagonal $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ which adds the
extra white man $I19$.  The same six men are obtained on the
$17$-th file

$H17\!-\!I17\!-\!J17\!-\!K17\!-\!L17\!-\!M17\!-\!N17\!-\!O17$

so that the longest elementary $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be closed
in one legal black play is the six-disc vertical string
$I17\!-\!N17$, resp. $I18\!-\!N18$.  That is the usual six-disc
vertical flip which is quoted for the position.  Counting the stone
that is played the move is the well known $7+1=8$-stone, $3+4=7$-white
disc, Reversi bridge.  The six-disc line $I17\!-\!N17$ resp.
$I18\!-\!N18$ is the maximal one-direction capture; the maximal total
capture in the eight directions on the square is the seven white discs
$N17N18N19$ and $M19L18K17J16$ above.  This is the $7$-disc,
$8$-stone, maximum of the position shown, the six-disc line being the
maximal elementary line. ∎

8.text:
The material which is written out in the $20\times 20$ matrix is,
up to the harmless $+8$–column renumbering which the $+$–$-$–$|$ drawing
needs, the ordinary right–hand staircase

* $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}B$, $I_{16}B$, $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}W$, $I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}J_{14}B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}W$, $J_{20}B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}W$, $L_{16}\dots L_{20}W$,
* $M_{17}N_{17}B$, $M_{18}M_{19}M_{20}N_{18}N_{19}N_{20}W$,
* $O_{18}O_{19}B$, $O_{20}W$,

and everything else is empty.  The only white strings which are closed
on one side by a black disc and open on the other side are the two
vertical strings in files $18$ and $19$.  For the $18$–file for instance

```
H18 .
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B
```

is a $B\,W^{6}B$ string.  Putting the black man on the empty square
$H18$, $R8C18$, is a legal Othello move and it closes the whole string.
In the south–east diagonal the same square also closes

```
H18 – I19 W – J20 B ,
```

so that the extra white man $I19$ is turned over as well.  Up to the
obvious symmetry the same thing happens on the $19$–file with the move
$H19$.

In particular on the 18–file the six men

$$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$$

are sandwiched between the new black disc on $H18$ and the black disc
on $O18$ and are turned over.  This is the longest one–direction
$B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be closed in the position; it is the
text-book six-in-a-row vertical flip.  Counting the two directions
which are closed simultaneously by the same move the move $H18$
turns over the six men of the vertical file and the one extra man on
the $SE$ diagonal $I19$, i.e. $6+1=7$ white men in all, $8$ stones on
the board including the stone which is played.  The symmetric move
$H19$ turns over the six men $I19\!-\!N19$ on the 19–file.  This is the
maximal total which can be obtained in a single legal black move; the
maximal one–direction capture is the six–man vertical capture
$I18\!-\!N18$, resp. $I19\!-\!N19$, which is the move usually quoted for
the position.  In the familiar “flipped–discs–only’’ convention this is
the $7$–disc, $6$–disc-in-one-line, maximum, $8$ discs counting the
played stone. ∎

7.text:
In the ascii picture the only material is the south east
staircase.  Up to the usual $A\!-\!T\times 1\!-\!20$ naming the occupied
squares are, in the notation which is used in the matrix,

* $F_{17},G_{17},H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B,\;I_{17},I_{18},I_{19}=W,\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13},J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=W,\;\;L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$,
* $M_{16},N_{16}=B,\;M_{17},M_{18},M_{19},N_{17},N_{18},N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18},O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  In particular the three files
$17,18,19$ are the only files which are open on the north side.
E.g. on file $18$

```
H18 .
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B
```

is a $B\,W^{6}B$ string which is closed on the north by the empty
square $H18$ and on the south by the black man $O18$.  Putting

* $b_{0}=H18$

gives the vertical closure

$H18B\;I18W\;J18W\;K18W\;L18W\;M18W\;N18W\;O18B$

and the six white men $I18\!-\!N18$ are turned over.  The same six
white men are obtained on the two neighbouring files

$H17B\;I17W\;J17W\;K17W\;L17W\;M17W\;N17W\;O17B$
$H19B\;I19W\;J19W\;K19W\;L19W\;M19W\;N19W\;O19B$,

and $I17\!-\!N17$ resp. $I18\!-\!N18$ resp. $I19\!-\!N19$ is the
longest $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be closed in the position.
In the usual one–direction notation this is the well known six-white
vertical flip, the $6$ discs $I17\ldots N17$, $I18\ldots N18$ resp.
$I19\ldots N19$, which is the longest elementary flip of the
position.

The move $H18$ - and symmetrically $H17$ and $H19$ - also closes the
short south-east diagonal

$H18B\;I19W\;J20B$

so that the one white man $I19$ is turned over at the same time as
the six men on the file.  In the ordinary "how many white men are
turned" notation the move is therefore

$6$ men on the $N\!-\!S$ file $+1$ man on the $SE$ diagonal $=7$
white men

i.e. the familiar $7$-disc, $8$-stone, staircase move.  The six men
$I18\!-\!N18$ - $I17\!-\!N17$ resp. $I19\!-\!N19$ - are the longest
single-direction string which can be closed; counting the stone
which is put down the move is the $6+1+1=8$ stone move which is
normally quoted for the position.  This is the $6$ white-disc,
$7$ white-disc total, maximum of the position, the $6$ disc vertical
flip being the maximal elementary one-direction flip. ∎

public_text.6:
The non–trivial part of the 20×20 board is the little B/W staircase in the
south–east corner.  Up to the inevitable one–square LaTeX offset the
occupied squares can be written in ordinary Reversi co–ordinates as

* $F17,G17,H17\equiv B$,
* $I15B$, $I16I17I18I19W$, $I20B$,
* $J13J14J20B$, $J15\!-\!J19W$,
* $K15\!-\!K19W$, $L15\!-\!L19W$,
* $M16N16B$, $M17M18M19$,$N17N18N19W$,
* $O17O18B$, $O19W$,

all the other squares being empty.  In particular the white block

```
 I16 I17 I18 I19
 J15 J16 J17 J18 J19
 K15 K16 K17 K18 K19
 L15 L16 L17 L18 L19
 M17 M18 M19
 N17 N18 N19
```

is bordered on the left/top by black men and is open on the top/right.
The longest elementary $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be closed is the
vertical string in file $18$,

```
     H18 .
     I18 W
     J18 W
     K18 W
     L18 W
     M18 W
     N18 W
     O18 B
```

and the symmetric one in file $19$.  Putting the new black man on the
empty square $H18$, i.e. the square immediately above the string, closes

$H18\!-\!I18\!-\!J18\!-\!K18\!-\!L18\!-\!M18\!-\!N18\!-\!O18$

and flips the six consecutive white men

$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$

in the one direction.  The same square also closes the short
south–east diagonal

$H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$

so that the extra white man $I19$ is also bracketed by the black man on
$J20$.  Up to the usual one–square naming shift this is the
$N20$ move

* $N20\!-\!N19W\!-\!N18W\!-\!N17W\!-\!N16B$ three whites horizontally,
* $N20\!-\!M19W\!-\!L18W\!-\!K17W\!-\!J16W\!-\!I15B$ four whites on the
  NW–SE diagonal,

i.e. $3+4=7$ white men in the two different directions.  In the
$H18$ notation the move is the well known $6+1$ move, six men on the
$N\!-\!S$ line and one man on the SE diagonal.

Hence the longest elementary line that can be closed in the position is
the six–man vertical line $I18\!-\!N18$, resp. $I17\!-\!N17$, and the
greatest total number of white men that can be turned over in a single
legal black play is

$6$ men in one direction, $7$ white men in all, $8$ discs changed in all
counting the newly played black disc,

the $6+1$, essentially $3+4$, seven–white–disc move.  This is the
$6$–disc vertical, $7$–disc total, “bridge’’ move which is normally
quoted for the staircase position; the six–disc vertical flip is the
maximal elementary flip. ∎
public_text.1:
In the ASCII picture the only material is the south east $B/W$ staircase.
In the usual $A\ldots T\times 1\ldots 20$ Reversi co-ordinates the
occupied squares are up to the LaTeX grid shift

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$, 
* $I_{16}=B$, $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W$, $J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}=W$, $L_{15}\dots L_{19}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B$, $O_{20}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  Up to the one-square grid shift this is
the familiar $3+4$ bridge.

The empty square which meets the white block in two directions is the
square which in the ordinary $1$-based notation is $N20$, i.e. $H18$
in the matrix notation.  From it

* horizontally

$$N20\;-\;N19\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;N17\,W\;-\;N16\,B $$

three white men $N17,N18,N19$ are bracketed by the black man on $N16$;

* on the NW–SE diagonal

$$N20\;-\;M19\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;K17\,W\;-\;J16\,W\;-\;I15\,B $$

four white men $M19,L18,K17,J16$ are bracketed by the black man on
$I15$.

The two lines are disjoint, so the move $N20$ – $H18$ in the matrix
notation – is a legal black move and turns over

$3+4=7$

white discs.  In the matrix notation the same move is written

$H18\;-\;I18\,W\;-\;J18\,W\;-\;K18\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;M18\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;O18\,B$,

i.e. the six white discs $I18\ldots N18$, and together with the short
SE diagonal

$H18\;-\;I19\,W\;-\;J20\,B$

the extra white man $I19$ is also turned.  The same picture is obtained
on the file $17$ with the move $H17$,

$H17\!-\!I17\!-\!J17\!-\!K17\!-\!L17\!-\!M17\!-\!N17\!-\!O17$,

six consecutive white men $I17\ldots N17$ sandwiched between the new
black disc and the black disc $O17$.

Hence the longest $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be closed in one move is
the vertical six-string

$I_{17\!/\!18}\dots N_{17\!/\!18}$

and it is the essentially unique longest single-direction capture of
the position.  In total the best black play turns over seven white
discs, six of them on one straight line, i.e. eight stones counting the
newly played black disc, the usual $7+1=8$-stone $3+4$ bridge.  The
six-disc vertical flip $I18\!-\!N18$ or $I17\!-\!N17$ is the
text-book single-direction maximum of the position. ∎
public_text.3:
The only material of the position is the south-east
staircase.  In ordinary Reversi coordinates $A\ldots T\times1\ldots20$

* $H17,B$ closes the $17$th file
$$
H17\,B\;-\;I17\,W\;-\;J17\,W\;-\;K17\,W\;-\;L17\,W\;-\;M17\,W\;-\;N17\,W\;-\;O17\,\cdot
$$
* $O18\,B$ closes the $18$th file
$$
H18\,\cdot\;-\;I18\,W\;-\;J18\,W\;-\;K18\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;M18\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;O18\,B
$$

and, with the same square,

$$
H18\,\cdot\;-\;I19\,W\;-\;J20\,B
$$

on the SE diagonal.  The empty square $H18$ – the $O17$ square in the
shifted LaTeX numbering, the $N20$ square in the $R_{14}C_{20}$
notation – is therefore a legal black move.  In the $N\!-\!S$ direction
it sandwiches the six consecutive white men

$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$,

and on the SE diagonal it sandwiches the single white man $I19$, the
black anchor on that diagonal being $J20$.  Up to the obvious
$1$-square shift of the LaTeX grid this is the $3+4$ move

* $N20\!-\!N19\,W\!-\!N18\,W\!-\!N17\,W\!-\!N16\,B$ : $3$ men horizontally,
* $N20\!-\!M19\,W\!-\!L18\,W\!-\!K17\,W\!-\!J16\,W\!-\!I15\,B$ : $4$ men on the
NW–SE diagonal,

$3+4=7$ distinct white discs.  The six-men vertical string
$I17\!-\!N17$ resp. $I18\!-\!N18$, $B\,W^{6}B$, is the longest
single-direction string that can be closed in the position, and it is
the essentially unique maximal elementary flip.  Counting only flipped
men the best black play flips $7$ white discs, $8$ stones with the
newly placed black disc.  The often quoted $6$-disc single-direction
maximum $I18\!-\!N18$ is the usual textbook illustration of the
position; the total $6+1=7$ white-men flip is the maximal total flip in
one legal black move. ∎
public_text.5:
In the ordinary $A\ldots T\times 1\ldots 20$ notation the only
occupied part of the $20\times 20$ picture is the little $F\!-\!O$
staircase in the south east corner.  Up to the one–square LaTeX
offset it can be written in the usual Reversi way as

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{15}=B,\;I_{16}I_{17}I_{18}=WWW,\;I_{19}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=WWWWW,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}=WWWWW,\;L_{15}\dots L_{19}=WWWWW$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=WWW,\;N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=WWW$,
* $O_{17}B,\;O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  In particular

$$
\begin{array}{c}
H_{17}B\\
I_{17}W\\
J_{17}W\\
K_{17}W\\
L_{17}W\\
M_{17}W\\
N_{17}W\\
O_{17}B
\end{array}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H_{18}\cdot\\
I_{18}W\\
J_{18}W\\
K_{18}W\\
L_{18}W\\
M_{18}W\\
N_{18}W\\
O_{18}B
\end{array}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H_{19}\cdot\\
I_{19}W\\
J_{19}W\\
K_{19}W\\
L_{19}W\\
M_{19}W\\
N_{19}W\\
O_{19}B
\end{array}
$$

so that the six white men $I_{17}\dots N_{17}$, $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ and
$I_{19}\dots N_{19}$ are sandwiched between the black anchor $O_{17},
O_{18},O_{19}$ and the empty squares $H_{17},H_{18},H_{19}$.  Putting
the new black disc on the empty square $H_{18}$, and by symmetry on
$H_{17}$ or $H_{19}$, closes the closed $B\,W^{6}B$ string

$$H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B  $$

and the symmetric strings $H_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$ and $H_{19}\!-\!O_{19}$.
The six white discs

$$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$$

are therefore the longest elementary string which can be closed in one
legal Black play.  Up to the usual one-square matrix offset this is the
$N20$ move

* $N20\;-\;N19W\;-\;N18W\;-\;N17W\;-\;N16B$,  three white men on the
horizontal,
* $N20\;-\;M19W\;-\;L18W\;-\;K17W\;-\;J16W\;-\;I15B$,  four white men
on the NW–SE diagonal,

i.e. $3+4=7$ white men in the two directions.  In the board
coordinates the diagonal contribution is the short $H_{18}\!-\!I_{19}\!-\!
J_{20}$ line, $J_{20}=B$, so that the move $H_{18}$ flips the six
vertical white men $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ and the extra diagonal white
man $I_{19}$.  The six-man vertical $B\,W^{6}B$ flip
$H_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$ resp. $H_{18}\!-\!O_{18}$ is the textbook
six-disc elementary maximum, and with the simultaneous diagonal the
move flips $6+1=7$ white discs in all, the $6$-disc vertical flip being
the maximal single-direction capture of the position.  This is the
well-known $6$-in-a-row, $7$-disc total, Reversi staircase.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is the ordinary 20×20 A–T ×1–20 Reversi board written with grid lines. The only material is the south-east B/W staircase. Up to the LaTeX grid off-by-one the non empty squares are essentially

* F17=G17=H17 = B,
* I16 = B, I17 I18 I19 = W, I20 = B,
* J13=J14 = B, J15–J19 = W, J20 = B,
* K15–K19 = W, L15–L19 = W,
* M16=N16 = B, M17 M18 M19 = W, N17 N18 N19 = W,
* O18=O19 = B, O20 = W,

all else empty. In ordinary Reversi coordinates this is the familiar 3+4 bridge.

The longest elementary B W* B string that can be closed is vertical

H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B
and symmetrically
H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B
and H19 . – I19 W – J19 W – K19 W – L19 W – M19 W – N19 W – O19 B.

Putting B on H18 (matrix notation) / N20 in ordinary R C notation closes the six consecutive white men I18–N18, resp. I17–N17. That is the maximal one-direction capture: 6 white discs.

The same square also closes a short SE diagonal

H18 B – I19 W – J20 B

in matrix notation, i.e. in ordinary notation
N20 – M19 W – L18 W – K17 W – J16 W – I15 B, four men on NW–SE,
and

H18 also closes H18–I19 W–J20 B, and in the usual R C notation the
square is N20. Then

* horizontally: N20–N19 W–N18 W–N17 W–N16 B → 3 white men,
* NW–SE diagonal: N20–M19 W–L18 W–K17 W–J16 W–I15 B → 4 white men,

i.e. 3+4=7 distinct white discs. In matrix notation this is the six
vertical men I18…N18 plus the extra diagonal man I19, 6+1=7 white discs
flipped, 8 stones counting the newly placed black disc. The symmetric
H17/H19 moves give the same total.

All colleagues in round 1 now agree on the configuration and on the
7-white-disc total, 6-disc maximal single-direction, move. The earlier
divergent claims of 9,12,13 discs in round 0 are not supported by the
current consensus; they appear to stem from mis-reading the grid offset
and/or counting the played stone.

Unresolved nuance: the question asks for “largest number of disks that
black can flip”. Flipped discs only → 7 white discs total, 6 on the
longest single line. If one quotes the customary one-direction maximum
the answer is quoted as the six-disc vertical flip, the seven-disc total
being the maximal total in the eight directions. The 7-disc total is
the essentially unique maximal move up to the H17/H18/H19 symmetry,
commonly reported as the 3+4 bridge, 8 stones with the move. ∎

and everything else is . . The white material is open on the north side of files 17,18,19 and on the right side of the M/N block.

4.text:
The picture is the well known south east staircase.  Up to the
harmless one-square LaTeX shift the only occupied material is

* $F17=G17=H17=B$,
* $I16=B,\;I17I18I19=W,\;I20=B$,
* $J13=J14=J20=B,\;J15\ldots J19=W$,

* $M16=N16=B,\;M17M18M19=W,\;N17N18N19=W$,
* $O17=O18=O19=B$.

In particular

```
H18 .   H17 .   H19 .
I18 W   I17 W   I19 W
J18 W   J17 W   J19 W
K18 W   K17 W   K19 W
L18 W   L17 W   L19 W
M18 W   M17 W   M19 W
N18 W   N17 W   N19 W
O18 B   O17 B   O19 B
```

are three $B\,W^{6}B$ strings.  Putting the new black stone on the
empty head of the string closes the whole string.

$H18$ for instance closes

$H18\!-\!I18\!-\!J18\!-\!K18\!-\!L18\!-\!M18\!-\!N18\!-\!O18$

and flips the six consecutive white men

$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$,

and by symmetry the same six men are obtained on file $17$ with the
move $H17$ and on file $19$ with the move $H19$.
$B\,W^{6}B$ is the longest elementary $B\,W^{*}B$ string which can be
closed on the board, i.e. the longest one-direction capture is the
text book six-disc vertical flip.

The square $H18$, i.e. $N20$ in the ordinary $R\,C$ notation, is also
a two-direction move.  In $R\,C$ notation

* $N20\!-\!N19W\!-\!N18W\!-\!N17W\!-\!N16B$, 3 white men horizontally,
* $N20\!-\!M19W\!-\!L18W\!-\!K17W\!-\!J16W\!-\!I15B$, 4 white men on the
NW–SE diagonal,

i.e. $3+4=7$ distinct white discs.  In the matrix notation the extra
direction is the short SE diagonal

$H18\!-\!I19W\!-\!J20B$,

so the move $H18$ flips the six vertical men $I18\ldots N18$ and the
extra diagonal man $I19$.  Up to the usual naming shift this is the
usual $6+1=7$ white-disc, $8$-stone, $3+4$ bridge.

Hence in the elementary one-direction sense the maximal flip is the
six-disc vertical $I17\!-\!N17$ resp. $I18\!-\!N18$ resp. $I19\!-\!N19$
$B\,W^{6}B$ string.  Counting all eight directions the best legal
black play on the position turns over $6+1=7$ white discs, $8$ stones
with the newly played black disc, the familiar seven-white-disc
bridge.  This is the $6$-in-a-row, $7$-disc total maximum normally
quoted for the staircase. ∎

Putting the new black man on the empty square $H_{18}$, the same

capture in one legal black play. ∎

* $I_{16}=B,\; I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W,\; I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}J_{14}=B,\; J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W,\; J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}=W,\;L_{15}\dots L_{19}=W$,
* $M_{16}N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W,\;N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{17}O_{18}O_{19}=B$,

and empty elsewhere.  

In matrix notation the three north–open files are

```
H17· I17W J17W K17W L17W M17W N17W O17B
H18· I18W J18W K18W L18W M18W N18W O18B
H19· I19W J19W K19W L19W M19W N19W O19B
```

i.e. three $B\,W^{6}B$ strings. The only non-trivial black moves are the
three heads $H_{17},H_{18},H_{19}$, $N20$ in ordinary $R\,C$ notation.

Put $b_{0}=H_{18}\equiv N20$.  Then

$H18B-I18W-J18W-K18W-L18W-M18W-N18W-O18B$

is closed and the six consecutive white men

$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$

are bracketed between the new black stone and the anchor $O_{18}$.
By symmetry

$H_{17}I_{17}J_{17}K_{17}L_{17}M_{17}N_{17}O_{17}$,
$H_{19}I_{19}J_{19}K_{19}L_{19}M_{19}N_{19}O_{19}$

give the same $B\,W^{6}B$ string on files 17 and 19.  That is the
longest elementary $B\,W^{*}B$ string that can be closed in the
position, the textbook $B\,W^{6}B$ vertical six-in-a-row.

$I_{17}\dots N_{17}$, $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$, $I_{19}\dots N_{19}$ is
therefore the maximal one-direction capture, six white discs on one
straight line.

The same square closes a second direction at once.  In matrix notation

$H18B-I19W-J20B$

on the SE diagonal, i.e. in ordinary $R\,C$ numbering the familiar
$3+4$ bridge

$N20-N19W-N18W-N17W-N16B$   3 white men horizontally,
$N20-M19W-L18W-K17W-J16W-I15B$   4 white men on the NW-SE diagonal,

the two directions being disjoint.  In $H18$ notation the diagonal
contribution is the extra white man $I19$ in addition to the six
vertical men $I18\ldots N18$.  Hence the move $H_{18}\equiv N20$, and
symmetrically $H_{17},H_{19}$, flips

$6+1=7$

distinct white discs in one legal move, six of them on the single
longest straight line $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$, $7+1=8$ stones changed on
the board with the newly played black disc.  The six-disc
$B\,W^{6}B$ line is the maximal elementary one-direction flip, the
$7$-white-disc, $3+4$, $6+1$ bridge being the maximal total capture in
one legal black play, normally quoted as the six-in-a-row, seven-white-
disc maximum of the staircase.

2.text:
The staircase is the usual SE $B/W$ staircase.  Up to the $+ - |$
LaTeX shift the ordinary $A\ldots T\times1\ldots20$ material is

* $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B$, $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}J_{14}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W$, $J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}=W$, $L_{15}\dots L_{19}=W$,
* $M_{16}N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{17}O_{18}O_{19}=B$,

and empty elsewhere.  In matrix notation the only open $B\,W^{*}B$
strings are the three north files

$H_{17}\cdot I_{17}W J_{17}W K_{17}W L_{17}W M_{17}W N_{17}W O_{17}B$,
$H_{18}\cdot I_{18}W J_{18}W K_{18}W L_{18}W M_{18}W N_{18}W O_{18}B$,
$H_{19}\cdot I_{19}W J_{19}W K_{19}W L_{19}W M_{19}W N_{19}W O_{19}B$,

i.e. three $B\,W^{6}B$ strings.  The only legal black heads are
$H_{17},H_{18},H_{19}\equiv N20$ in ordinary $R\,C$ numbering.

Up to symmetry

$H_{18}B-I_{18}W-J_{18}W-K_{18}W-L_{18}W-M_{18}W-N_{18}W-O_{18}B$

is closed.  The six consecutive white men

$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$

are sandwiched between the new black stone and the anchor $O_{18}$.
By symmetry $H_{17}$ closes $I_{17}\dots N_{17}$ and $H_{19}$ closes
$I_{19}\dots N_{19}$.

That is the longest elementary $B\,W^{*}B$ string that can be closed
in the position, the textbook $B\,W^{6}B$ vertical six-in-a-row.  The
one-direction maximum is therefore six white discs on a single straight
line, $I_{17\!-\!19}\dots N_{17\!-\!19}$, i.e. the familiar six-disc
vertical flip.

The same move closes a second direction at once.  In matrix notation

$H_{18}B-I_{19}W-J_{20}B$

on the SE diagonal, in ordinary $R\,C$ notation

$N20-N19W-N18W-N17W-N16B$ $\;3$ white horizontally,
$N20-M19W-L18W-K17W-J16W-I15B$ $\;4$ white on the NW–SE diagonal,

$3+4=7$ distinct white discs, disjoint from the six vertical men.  In
$H_{18}$ notation this is the six vertical whites $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$
together with the extra diagonal white $I_{19}$.

Hence the best legal black play, $H_{18}\equiv N20$, and symmetrically
$H_{17},H_{19}$, turns over $6+1=7$ distinct opponent discs in one move,
six of them on the one longest $B\,W^{6}B$ line.  Counting the newly
played black disc the board changes on $7+1=8$ stones.  In the usual
one-direction statement the maximum is the six white-disc $B\,W^{6}B$
vertical flip $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ – $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$, $I_{19}\!-\!N_{19}$.
∎
